curated.tagline: A shared field journal for any crew — native iOS built and deployed entirely on Linux via xtool
curated.description: Kate is a field journal for crews and small groups: journal entries with photos, hangout ideas, a movie shelf, places and outings with live GPS tracks, and week windows that find when everyone's free. The iOS client is pure SwiftUI + SwiftPM with zero third-party dependencies — signed, compiled, and installed from Arch Linux ARM via xtool, no Xcode machine required. A typed API on Cloudflare Workers (D1 + R2) keeps every member's view in sync: anyone can sign up and start a crew, members join by invitation, and writes queue in an offline outbox.

release.transcript: A launch film for Kate, the shared field journal for crews and small groups, with native iOS built on Linux.

showcase.whatItIs: A shared field journal for the spontaneous things a crew does together: journal entries with photos, hangout ideas, a movie shelf, places and outings, and week windows that find when everyone is free.
showcase.whoItsFor: Any small group or household that wants one shared log. Anyone can sign up at kate.shippedit.dev and start a crew; members join by invitation.
showcase.whatLukeBuilt: A native iOS client in pure SwiftUI and SwiftPM with no third-party dependencies, signed, built and installed from Linux with xtool. A typed API on Cloudflare Workers with D1 and R2 keeps every member's view in sync, with an offline outbox for writes.
showcase.status: Live with open sign-up. The site and API run on Cloudflare Workers; the iOS app is the main client and is being prepared for the App Store.
showcase.problem: Shared group memories end up scattered across chat threads, camera rolls and notes, and a planning app built for one household does not fit a crew whose members come and go. Kate started as a two-person journal and had to become something any small group could run.
showcase.approach: Journal entries are the core and every other module (ideas, movies, places, availability) hangs off the same crew and member model. Growth is by invitation with a per-member invite budget, and the whole server can be self-hosted on a free Cloudflare account so a crew never has to live on the hosted instance.
showcase.architecture: A Next.js app on Cloudflare Workers (via OpenNext) serves a typed v1 API backed by D1 for records and R2 for photos. The iOS client is pure SwiftUI/SwiftPM with one shared API client and an offline outbox that queues journal entries and ideas until the network returns. A generated design-token file keeps colours and sizes in one place across web and iOS.
showcase.outcomes: Open sign-up works with Sign in with Apple or pairing code, crews have invites and a waitlist, and the same API serves the hosted and self-hosted deployments. The iOS app builds, signs and installs from Linux with xtool and is being prepared for App Store submission.

highlights: Native iOS built end-to-end on Linux — xtool signs and deploys
Zero-dependency SwiftUI client, Linux-tested pure core
Crew model — members, colors, and ratings come from the API
Offline outbox for journal and idea writes
curated.architecture: SwiftUI tabs → KateStore/KateCore client → Cloudflare Worker /api/v1 → D1 + R2 media → per-member sync
